intro: At C1 you combined several sources into one summary, organised by theme, with every claim attributed. At C2 the sources are longer and they argue with each other: you'll map each one, find where the real debate lies, retell each argument without bending it, and boil one long text down to a short, exact précis. Warm-up: think of a report or article you had to summarise at work or university. What was the hardest thing to keep?
teachingNotes: Mediation lesson (strand ME: helping other people understand a text or each other). Build on the chain and recap each in a line, don't re-teach: c1-mediation-synthesis (synthesis by theme, not source by source; Both sources agree … / …, whereas … / Neither source mentions …; attribution, reporting both figures with their sources; translating the meaning of Indonesian bureaucratic terms: sosialisasi → an awareness campaign, ditindaklanjuti → followed up), c1-reading-complex (claim, reasons, evidence, counter-argument, rebuttal; loaded words; correlation vs causation) and, outside the chain but done, c1-hedging (may / tend to / appear to; suggests, not proves), c1-academic-writing (paraphrase keeps hedges and scope; argues, claims, notes, points out) and c1-academic-vocabulary (acknowledge, dispute, assert, imply). New here: mapping long sources and explaining WHY they conflict, stance verbs (maintain, concede, reject, caution, question), reconstructing arguments faithfully (structure, hedges, scope, counter-arguments; the straw man) and the précis. Every source extract is an invented practice text: never present its figures as real statistics or attribute them to a real ministry, institute, newspaper or association. (Jakarta's odd-even rule, ganjil-genap, is real; the congestion-fee sources and figures are invented.)

Summarising several sources (summarise-sources). Method: 1) map each source: claim, evidence, stance (for / against / mixed, and how certain); 2) find the debate: where they agree, where they conflict and WHY (different evidence, different priorities or values, different scope or time frame); 3) write by issue, attributing every claim. Stance verbs: argues (gives reasons: the neutral default), maintains / insists (holds a position firmly, often against criticism), concedes / acknowledges / accepts (grants a point that goes against its own side), rejects / disputes (says a view or a figure is wrong; they take a noun: rejects the view that …), cautions / warns (points to a risk; cautions that … / cautions against + -ing), questions (doubts: questions whether …), suggests (tentative), notes / observes (neutral). Verbs and words that smuggle in the summariser's view: claims (can signal doubt), admits (sounds like a confession), shows / proves / demonstrates / points out / refutes (the summariser accepts it as true), rightly, wrongly, sensibly, convincingly, fails to, simply ignores. No own view unless the task asks; then put it after the summary, clearly marked (In my view, …). Indonesian traps: mengatakan for everything → says for everything (correct but flat); mengakui → admits (confession) where acknowledges / concedes is meant; membantah → denies (an accusation or a fact) vs rejects / disputes (a view or a figure); menurut saya slipping into the middle of a summary.

Reconstructing arguments (reconstruct-arguments). The test: would the author say 'Yes, that's what I said'? Keep 1) the logical shape: claim + reason (because) + condition (unless, if, only if, until): 'pause X until Y' is not 'ban X'; 2) hedges at the same strength: may contribute to ≠ causes, appears to ≠ shows, tends to ≠ always, some ≠ most, and don't weaken firm claims either (will ≠ might); 3) qualifications and scope: for under-25s, in urban areas, in the first year, at the 12 startups in the trial; 4) the counter-arguments the source itself answers (The author acknowledges that … but argues that …); 5) only the evidence the source gives (don't 'improve' an argument). Straw man (orang-orangan sawah) = retelling an argument as a weaker or more extreme version that is easy to knock down; a misrepresentation even when accidental. Indonesian traps: bisa covers can / may / could and sometimes will, so 'bisa menyebabkan' in a source is a hedge (may / can cause), never 'causes'; cenderung = tends to, keep it; semua / selalu creeping in where the source said banyak / sering.

The précis (write-precis). From French, said PRAY-see (plural the same, said PRAY-seez; also written precis). A short, accurate summary of ONE text in your own words (a synthesis combines several). Length: often about a quarter to a third of the original; a word count in the task always wins. Main points in the same order and proportion as the original (be honest that some university guides allow regrouping when it shows the argument more clearly: follow the task). Leave out examples, anecdotes, quotations, repetition and the writer's own opinions. Third person; present tense for what the text says (The author argues …, The report concludes …); past is normal for what a study did (The researchers surveyed …). Key technical terms and names may stay. Method: read (twice) → underline the thesis and main points → outline → draft from the outline without looking → cut (examples, repetition, detail) → check against the original (meaning, hedges, scope, order, length). Don't open every sentence with According to the author: say it once, then She adds … / She concludes …. Indonesian habit: a school ringkasan often copies key sentences from each paragraph; a précis is rewritten.

C2 honesty and grading: many choices here are style (argues / maintains / contends, cautions / warns, concedes / acknowledges, a quarter or a third). Accept any accurate wording and only mark clear faults: a stance verb that contradicts what the source does (concedes for a rejection, rejects for a warning), a strengthened, weakened or dropped hedge, a dropped qualification or condition that changes the claim, the summariser's opinion inside the summary, a straw man, a précis with examples, quotations or opinions, or far off the length. When the learner writes a summary or précis, check meaning first (hedges, scope, conditions), then organisation (by issue, same order), then ONE language point; react to the content before correcting.

Limits: every structure is available at C2; the point is accuracy and control, not new grammar. Don't teach citation styles (APA etc. belong to c1-academic-writing), formal logic, lists of named fallacies beyond the straw man, or statistics. Practice: play a manager, lecturer or editor who asks for a summary of two or three short invented texts from the learner's field (ministries, NGOs, startups, universities in Jakarta, Bandung, Surabaya, Yogyakarta), or ask for a précis of a short text you write; keep figures invented and labelled as practice.

keyPoints.title: Map the sources, then summarise the debate
keyPoints.explanation: First map each source: its claim, its evidence and its stance (for, against or mixed, and how sure). Then find the debate: where the sources agree, where they conflict and why (different evidence, priorities or scope). Write by issue, attribute every claim and choose a reporting verb that matches the stance: argues, maintains, concedes, rejects, cautions, questions. Keep your own view out unless you're asked for it.

examples.en: The sources agree on the problem but not on the solution.
examples.id: Sumber-sumber itu sepakat soal masalahnya, tapi tidak soal solusinya.

examples.en: The union acknowledges that the company is losing money, but argues that job cuts are not the answer.
examples.id: Serikat pekerja mengakui bahwa perusahaan sedang merugi, tapi berargumen bahwa PHK bukan jawabannya.

examples.en: The researchers caution against drawing conclusions from one year of data.
examples.id: Para peneliti mengingatkan agar tidak menarik kesimpulan dari data satu tahun saja.

id.title: Petakan sumbernya, lalu ringkas perdebatannya
id.explanation: Pertama, petakan tiap sumber: klaimnya, buktinya dan sikapnya (mendukung, menolak atau campuran, dan seberapa yakin). Lalu temukan perdebatannya: di mana sumber-sumber itu sepakat, di mana bertentangan dan kenapa (bukti, prioritas atau cakupan yang berbeda). Tulis per persoalan, sebutkan sumber setiap klaim dan pilih kata kerja pelapor yang sesuai dengan sikapnya: argues, maintains, concedes, rejects, cautions, questions. Jangan masukkan pendapatmu sendiri kecuali diminta.

keyPoints.title: Rebuild each argument without bending it
keyPoints.explanation: Keep the argument's shape: the claim, the reason (because) and the condition (unless, only if, until). Keep hedges at the same strength: may contribute to is not causes, appears to is not shows. Keep the qualifications and scope (for under-25s, in urban areas, in the first year) and the counter-argument the source answers. A straw man, a weaker or more extreme version of someone's argument, is a misrepresentation even when it's accidental.

examples.en: The study suggests that longer commutes may contribute to staff turnover.
examples.id: Studi itu mengindikasikan bahwa perjalanan kerja yang lebih lama mungkin ikut menyebabkan tingginya pergantian karyawan.

examples.en: The author supports the merger, but only if no jobs are lost.
examples.id: Penulis mendukung merger itu, tapi hanya jika tidak ada yang kehilangan pekerjaan.

examples.en: She acknowledges that the sample was small, but maintains that the trend is clear.
examples.id: Dia mengakui bahwa sampelnya kecil, tapi tetap berpendapat bahwa trennya jelas.

id.title: Susun ulang tiap argumen tanpa membelokkannya
id.explanation: Pertahankan bentuk argumennya: klaim, alasan (because) dan syarat (unless, only if, until). Pertahankan kata pelunak dengan kekuatan yang sama: may contribute to bukan causes, appears to bukan shows. Pertahankan batasan dan cakupannya (for under-25s, in urban areas, in the first year) serta argumen tandingan yang dijawab sumber itu. Straw man, yaitu versi argumen orang lain yang dibuat lebih lemah atau lebih ekstrem, tetap merupakan penggambaran yang keliru walaupun tidak disengaja.

keyPoints.title: Write a précis: short, faithful, in your own words
keyPoints.explanation: A précis is a short, accurate summary of one text: often about a quarter to a third of the original, with its main points in the same order and proportion. Leave out examples, quotations and your own opinions. Write in the third person and use the present tense for the text's claims (The author argues …). Method: read, underline the thesis and main points, outline, draft, cut, then check against the original.

examples.en: The article argues that online learning works best when it is combined with face-to-face classes.
examples.id: Artikel itu berargumen bahwa pembelajaran daring paling efektif bila digabung dengan kelas tatap muka.

examples.en: The report concludes that the programme should continue, provided that funding is secured.
examples.id: Laporan itu menyimpulkan bahwa program tersebut sebaiknya dilanjutkan, asalkan dananya terjamin.

examples.en: She adds that teachers will need at least a year of training.
examples.id: Dia menambahkan bahwa para guru akan butuh pelatihan setidaknya satu tahun.

id.title: Menulis précis: pendek, setia pada aslinya, dengan kata-katamu sendiri
id.explanation: Précis adalah ringkasan pendek dan akurat dari satu teks: sering kira-kira seperempat sampai sepertiga panjang aslinya, dengan poin-poin utama dalam urutan dan proporsi yang sama. Buang contoh, kutipan dan pendapatmu sendiri. Tulis dengan sudut pandang orang ketiga dan pakai present tense untuk klaim teksnya (The author argues …). Caranya: baca, garis bawahi tesis dan poin-poin utama, buat kerangka, tulis draf, pangkas, lalu cek lagi dengan teks aslinya.

guidedPractice.prompt: Source C (a practice text) says: 'We are not convinced that a survey of 40 drivers tells us much about 30,000 drivers.' Complete the summary with one verb (= mempertanyakan): The association ___ whether a survey of 40 drivers is enough.
guidedPractice.hint: questions whether … = mempertanyakan apakah …: the source doubts something, but doesn't say it's wrong.

guidedPractice.prompt: Three practice sources discuss a new school-zoning rule in Bandung. Not one of them talks about the cost for parents. Complete with one word: ___ of the three sources mentions the cost for parents.
guidedPractice.hint: For a gap in three or more sources: None of the sources mentions … (for two sources: Neither source mentions …).

guidedPractice.prompt: A practice report says: 'Remote work tends to suit experienced staff better than new graduates.' Your summary must keep the hedge. Complete with two words: The report finds that remote work ___ suit experienced staff better than new graduates.
guidedPractice.hint: tends to = cenderung. Without it, the summary says remote work ALWAYS suits experienced staff better: a stronger claim than the source makes.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with one word: A précis leaves out examples, quotations and your own ___.
guidedPractice.hint: A précis restates the text faithfully: no anecdotes, no quotations and no evaluation of your own.

independentPractice.prompt: A practice article says: 'The new toll road will ease traffic, unless more housing is built along it.' A summary says: 'The author argues that the toll road will ease traffic.' Type the word that introduced the condition the summary dropped.
independentPractice.hint: unless = kecuali jika. Without the condition, the author seems to promise less traffic in every case.

independentPractice.prompt: Complete with one word: In a précis you write about the text in the ___ person: The author argues …, She concludes …
independentPractice.hint: Third person = he, she, it, they, the author. Not I (first person) and not you (second person).

independentPractice.prompt: Despite heavy criticism, a minister keeps repeating in a practice statement: 'The policy is working.' Complete with one verb (= tetap berpendapat): The minister ___ that the policy is working.
independentPractice.hint: maintains that … = tetap berpendapat bahwa …: holds a position firmly, often against criticism.

assessment.prompt: Practice text (invented). A traders' association in Bandung responds to a plan to ban single-use plastic bags in markets: 'We accept that plastic waste is a serious problem in the city. But paper bags cost three times as much, and our members' margins are already thin.' Choose the best verb from this list: concedes, rejects, cautions. Summary: 'The traders' association ___ that plastic waste is a serious problem, but argues that paper bags would cost its members three times as much.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: concedes (= mengakui: the association grants a point that supports the other side before giving its own argument). 'acknowledges', 'accepts', 'grants', 'recognises' = 100 (same stance; not in the list but accurate). 'concede' without -s or 'conceded' = 80 (right verb; the summary uses the present for the source's claims). 'admits' = 60 (right direction, but it sounds like a confession of something wrong). 'agrees' = 70. 'says' or 'states' = 40 (neutral but hides the stance). 'rejects' = 0 (the opposite: the association accepts the point). 'cautions' = 10 (it isn't warning about a risk here).

assessment.prompt: Practice text (invented). An environmental group writes about the same plastic-bag ban: 'Some say the ban will hurt small traders. This is simply not true: the city will give every trader free cloth bags for the first six months.' Choose the best verb from this list: concedes, rejects, maintains. Summary: 'The environmental group ___ the view that the ban will hurt small traders, pointing to the city's plan to hand out free cloth bags.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: rejects (= menolak: the group says the view is wrong; reject takes a noun: rejects the view that …). 'disputes', 'dismisses', 'challenges', 'contests' = 100. 'denies' = 70 (understandable, but deny is usually for an accusation or a fact, not a view). 'reject' / 'rejected' = 80. 'refutes' = 50 (it means 'proves wrong', so the summariser agrees with the group: not neutral). 'concedes' = 0 (the opposite stance). 'maintains' = 0 (it would mean the group holds that view).

assessment.prompt: You're writing a neutral summary of three practice sources about the plastic-bag ban. Your manager wants the sources' views only, not yours. Type the ONE word in this sentence that adds your own opinion and should be cut: 'The university study rightly cautions that a ban without cheap alternatives could push traders back to plastic within a year.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: rightly (it says the summariser agrees with the study; a neutral summary only reports the source's stance). 'cautions' = 0 (it reports the study's own stance, a warning, so it belongs in a neutral summary). 'could' = 0 (the study's own hedge: it must stay). 'cheap' = 0 (part of the study's claim). Two or more words including 'rightly' = 60.

assessment.prompt: A practice transport study (invented) says: 'In Surabaya, the growth of ride-hailing apps may contribute to falling bus use.' A colleague's summary says: 'The study finds that ride-hailing apps cause falling bus use in Surabaya.' Type the words from the original that should replace 'cause', so the summary keeps the study's hedge (three words).
assessment.rubric: Correct: may contribute to (= mungkin ikut menyebabkan: 'may' keeps it uncertain, and 'contribute to' makes the apps one factor among others; 'cause' turns a cautious finding into a proven, single cause). 'may contribute' = 90. 'might contribute to' / 'could contribute to' = 80 (the same hedge, but not the original's words). 'may cause' = 50 (keeps the uncertainty but loses 'one factor among others'). 'contribute to' = 40 (drops may). 'causes' or 'cause' = 0.

assessment.prompt: A practice report by an HR consultancy in Jakarta (invented) says: 'Among employees under 30, the four-day week improved staff retention by 12%.' A summary says: 'The report finds that the four-day week improved staff retention by 12%.' Type the qualification the summary dropped (the group the finding is about).
assessment.rubric: Correct: among employees under 30 (the finding is only about this age group; without it, the summary claims the result for all staff). 'under 30', 'employees under 30', 'under-30s' and similar = 100. 'young employees' / 'young staff' = 70 (right idea, but loses the exact limit of 30). 'by 12%' = 0 (that wasn't dropped). 'among employees' alone = 20 (misses the age limit, which is the point).

assessment.prompt: Your lecturer in Yogyakarta asks for a précis of a 1,200-word practice article on water policy and gives no word count. Choose the most suitable length from this list: 100 words, 350 words, 900 words.
assessment.rubric: Correct: 350 words (a précis is often about a quarter to a third of the original: 300–400 words for 1,200). '300' or '400' = 100 if the learner gives a number in that range instead of choosing. '100 words' = 20 (less than a tenth: too short to keep the main points in proportion). '900 words' = 0 (three-quarters of the original: hardly a summary).

assessment.prompt: You're writing a précis of a practice opinion article. Complete with the correct form of 'argue' for a précis: 'The author ___ that Indonesian cities should build fewer flyovers and more bus lanes.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: argues (a précis reports what the text says in the present tense, third person: the text still says it). 'argued' = 50 (the past is possible in some summaries, but a précis normally uses the present for the text's claims). 'is arguing' = 30 (not used for reporting a text's position). 'argue' = 20 (missing -s for 'the author'). A different verb such as 'maintains' or 'claims' = 40 (the task asks for a form of 'argue').

material.title: Several complex sources: map them, then find the debate

blocks.text:
Quick recap: at C1 you wrote a **synthesis** (one text from several sources) **by theme, not source by source**, with **attribution** (*According to the NGO's survey, …*), and from complex reading you can find a text's **claim, reasons, evidence, counter-argument and rebuttal**. At C2 the sources are long and they **argue with each other**. Before you write a word, **map** them.

**Step 1: map each source.** For every source, note three things:
- **Claim:** what it says is true or should happen.
- **Evidence:** what it bases that on (a model, a survey, an example, a principle).
- **Stance** (sikap): for, against or mixed, and **how sure** it is (*will* or *may*?).

**Step 2: find the debate.** Where do the sources **agree**? Where do they **conflict**? And **why** do they conflict? Usually for one of three reasons:
- **different evidence** (two surveys, two figures);
- **different priorities or values** (traffic vs fairness, cost vs quality);
- **different scope** (cakupan: one looks at the city centre, another at the suburbs; one at the first year, another at ten years).

**Step 3: write by issue.** One paragraph per issue (persoalan), with each source's position on it and a reporting verb that shows its stance (next section). **Your own view stays out** unless the task asks for it; if it does, put it at the end and mark it clearly (*In my view, …*).

id.text:
Ulasan singkat: di C1 kamu menulis **sintesis** (satu teks dari beberapa sumber) **per tema, bukan per sumber**, dengan **atribusi** (menyebut siapa yang bilang: *According to the NGO's survey, …*), dan dari pelajaran membaca teks kompleks kamu bisa menemukan **klaim, alasan, bukti, argumen tandingan dan bantahan** sebuah teks. Di C2 sumbernya panjang dan **saling berdebat**. Sebelum menulis satu kata pun, **petakan** dulu.

**Langkah 1: petakan tiap sumber.** Untuk setiap sumber, catat tiga hal:
- **Klaim:** apa yang menurutnya benar atau harus terjadi.
- **Bukti:** apa dasarnya (model, survei, contoh, prinsip).
- **Sikap** (*stance*): mendukung, menolak atau campuran, dan **seberapa yakin** (*will* atau *may*?).

**Langkah 2: temukan perdebatannya.** Di mana sumber-sumber itu **sepakat**? Di mana mereka **bertentangan**? Dan **kenapa** bertentangan? Biasanya karena salah satu dari tiga alasan:
- **bukti yang berbeda** (dua survei, dua angka);
- **prioritas atau nilai yang berbeda** (kemacetan vs keadilan, biaya vs kualitas);
- **cakupan yang berbeda** (*scope*: satu melihat pusat kota, yang lain pinggiran; satu melihat tahun pertama, yang lain sepuluh tahun).

**Langkah 3: tulis per persoalan.** Satu paragraf per persoalan (*issue*), berisi posisi tiap sumber tentang hal itu dan kata kerja pelapor yang menunjukkan sikapnya (bagian berikutnya). **Pendapatmu sendiri tidak masuk** kecuali tugasnya memintanya; kalau diminta, taruh di akhir dan tandai dengan jelas (*In my view, …*).

blocks.text:
Three practice sources (all invented) on a plan to charge cars entering central Jakarta at peak times, a **congestion fee** (biaya kemacetan; the city already uses the odd-even number-plate rule, *ganjil-genap*):
- **Source A**, a report by an urban research institute: *Our traffic model shows that a fee is likely to cut peak-hour traffic in the centre by 15–20% in its first year. The city should phase it in, however: a sudden start could push cars onto side streets.*
- **Source B**, an economist's column: *A congestion fee is fair: drivers should pay for the road space they use, and cities that charge drivers usually see fewer cars at peak times. The claim that the fee would hurt low-income workers is wrong: most of them travel by bus or motorbike, which would be exempt.*
- **Source C**, a statement from an online drivers' association: *We accept that a fee may reduce traffic. But online car drivers would pay up to Rp 600,000 a month, and nobody has asked us.*

The map: all three expect **less traffic**, so that's agreement. The conflict is about **who pays**: B says low-income workers won't, C says its drivers will. **Why** they conflict: **scope**. B is thinking of people who commute by bus or motorbike, C of people who drive for a living. A synthesis, by issue:

id.text:
Tiga sumber latihan (semuanya karangan) tentang rencana menarik biaya dari mobil yang masuk pusat Jakarta pada jam sibuk, yaitu **congestion fee** (biaya kemacetan; kota itu sudah memakai aturan pelat nomor ganjil-genap, *odd-even rule*):
- **Sumber A**, laporan sebuah lembaga riset perkotaan: *Our traffic model shows that a fee is likely to cut peak-hour traffic in the centre by 15–20% in its first year. The city should phase it in, however: a sudden start could push cars onto side streets.*
- **Sumber B**, kolom seorang ekonom: *A congestion fee is fair: drivers should pay for the road space they use, and cities that charge drivers usually see fewer cars at peak times. The claim that the fee would hurt low-income workers is wrong: most of them travel by bus or motorbike, which would be exempt.*
- **Sumber C**, pernyataan sebuah asosiasi pengemudi online: *We accept that a fee may reduce traffic. But online car drivers would pay up to Rp 600,000 a month, and nobody has asked us.*

Petanya: ketiganya memperkirakan **lalu lintas berkurang**, jadi itu kesamaannya. Pertentangannya soal **siapa yang membayar**: B bilang pekerja berpenghasilan rendah tidak akan membayar, C bilang pengemudinya akan membayar. **Kenapa** bertentangan: **cakupan**. B memikirkan orang yang pergi kerja naik bus atau motor, C memikirkan orang yang mencari nafkah dengan menyetir. Sintesisnya, per persoalan:

rows.en: All three sources expect a congestion fee to reduce traffic in central Jakarta.
rows.id: Ketiga sumber memperkirakan biaya kemacetan akan mengurangi lalu lintas di pusat Jakarta.

rows.en: The institute's model puts the fall at 15–20% in the first year, though it cautions that a sudden start could push cars onto side streets.
rows.id: Model lembaga itu memperkirakan penurunannya 15–20% pada tahun pertama, meskipun lembaga itu mengingatkan bahwa penerapan mendadak bisa mendorong mobil ke jalan-jalan kecil.
rows.note: a claim and the source's own warning

id.note: klaim dan peringatan dari sumber itu sendiri

rows.en: They disagree on who would bear the cost: the economist argues that low-income workers would be exempt, whereas the drivers' association says its members would pay up to Rp 600,000 a month.
rows.id: Mereka berbeda pendapat soal siapa yang akan menanggung biayanya: ekonom itu berargumen bahwa pekerja berpenghasilan rendah akan dibebaskan, sedangkan asosiasi pengemudi mengatakan anggotanya akan membayar hingga Rp600.000 per bulan.

rows.en: The difference is largely one of scope: the economist has commuters in mind, the association people who drive for a living.
rows.id: Perbedaannya sebagian besar soal cakupan: ekonom itu memikirkan para komuter, asosiasi itu memikirkan orang yang mencari nafkah dengan menyetir.

rows.en: Neither the institute nor the economist mentions online drivers.
rows.id: Baik lembaga itu maupun ekonom itu tidak menyebut pengemudi online.

blocks.text:
Common mistakes:
- **Source by source:** three mini-summaries, and the reader has to find the debate alone.
- **Every verb is *says*:** the reader can't tell who supports, who doubts and who warns. In Indonesian, *mengatakan* or *menyebutkan* covers a lot; in an English summary, the verb carries the stance.
- **Your opinion sneaks in:** *rightly, sensibly, convincingly, fails to see, simply ignores*. These words judge the source. Cut them, or move your view to a separate, clearly marked paragraph.
- **Inventing agreement or conflict:** if a source doesn't mention an issue, say so (*Source C doesn't address …*); don't guess its position.

id.text:
Kesalahan umum:
- **Per sumber:** tiga ringkasan mini, dan pembaca harus mencari sendiri perdebatannya.
- **Semua kata kerjanya *says*:** pembaca tidak bisa tahu siapa yang mendukung, siapa yang ragu dan siapa yang memperingatkan. Dalam bahasa Indonesia, *mengatakan* atau *menyebutkan* mencakup banyak hal; dalam ringkasan bahasa Inggris, kata kerjanya yang membawa sikap.
- **Pendapatmu menyusup:** *rightly, sensibly, convincingly, fails to see, simply ignores*. Kata-kata ini menilai sumbernya. Buang, atau pindahkan pendapatmu ke paragraf terpisah yang ditandai dengan jelas.
- **Mengarang kesepakatan atau pertentangan:** kalau sebuah sumber tidak membahas suatu persoalan, katakan begitu (*Source C doesn't address …*); jangan menebak posisinya.

blocks.prompt: A practice summary of the three congestion-fee sources says: 'The economist sensibly argues that the fee is fair, and the drivers simply ignore the benefits.' What is the main problem?
options: It adds the summariser's own judgement.
blocks.explain: *sensibly* and *simply ignore* are the **summariser's judgement**, not the sources' views. They also misrepresent Source C, which actually **accepts** that the fee may reduce traffic. Being organised by issue is a good thing, and *argues* is a reporting verb.

id.prompt: Sebuah ringkasan latihan dari tiga sumber tentang biaya kemacetan berbunyi: 'The economist sensibly argues that the fee is fair, and the drivers simply ignore the benefits.' Apa masalah utamanya?

Keduanya juga menggambarkan Sumber C secara keliru, padahal sumber itu justru **mengakui** bahwa biaya itu mungkin mengurangi kemacetan. Tersusun per persoalan itu hal yang baik, dan *argues* adalah kata kerja pelapor.

material.title: Reporting verbs that carry the stance

blocks.text:
From academic vocabulary you know **argue, claim, suggest, acknowledge, dispute, note**. In a summary of a debate these verbs do the job that tone of voice does in speech: they tell the reader **where each source stands**. Choose by what the source actually does:
- **argues** (berargumen): gives reasons for a view. The safe, neutral default.
- **maintains / insists** (tetap berpendapat / bersikeras): holds a position firmly, often against criticism.
- **concedes / acknowledges / accepts** (mengakui): grants a point that goes **against its own side**: *The association concedes that a fee may reduce traffic, but …*
- **rejects / disputes** (menolak / membantah): says a view or a figure is wrong: *The economist rejects the claim that …*
- **cautions / warns** (mengingatkan / memperingatkan): points to a risk: *The institute cautions that … / cautions against introducing it too quickly*.
- **questions** (mempertanyakan): doubts something: *The association questions whether …*
- **suggests** (mengindikasikan): a careful, tentative claim. **notes / observes** (mencatat): neutral.

**Words that carry YOUR view**, so use them only when you mean it:
- **claims** can sound as if you doubt the source.
- **admits** suggests something embarrassing or wrong (*He admitted taking the money*). For a fair point granted in a debate, **concedes** or **acknowledges** is neutral.
- **shows, proves, demonstrates, points out, refutes** say that **you** accept it's true (*refutes* = proves it wrong).
- **rightly, wrongly, convincingly, fails to** judge the source openly.

Grammar: *reject* and *dispute* usually take a noun (*rejects the view that …, disputes the figure*); *caution* takes *that* or *against* + -ing; *question* takes *whether* or a noun.

id.text:
Dari pelajaran kosakata akademik kamu sudah tahu **argue, claim, suggest, acknowledge, dispute, note**. Dalam ringkasan sebuah perdebatan, kata-kata kerja ini melakukan tugas yang dalam percakapan dilakukan oleh nada suara: memberi tahu pembaca **di mana posisi tiap sumber**. Pilih berdasarkan apa yang benar-benar dilakukan sumber itu:
- **argues** (berargumen): memberi alasan untuk sebuah pandangan. Pilihan aman dan netral.
- **maintains / insists** (tetap berpendapat / bersikeras): mempertahankan posisi dengan kuat, sering meski dikritik.
- **concedes / acknowledges / accepts** (mengakui): menerima satu poin yang justru **menguntungkan pihak lain**: *The association concedes that a fee may reduce traffic, but …*
- **rejects / disputes** (menolak / membantah): mengatakan sebuah pandangan atau angka salah: *The economist rejects the claim that …*
- **cautions / warns** (mengingatkan / memperingatkan): menunjuk sebuah risiko: *The institute cautions that … / cautions against introducing it too quickly*.
- **questions** (mempertanyakan): meragukan sesuatu: *The association questions whether …*
- **suggests** (mengindikasikan): klaim yang hati-hati. **notes / observes** (mencatat): netral.

**Kata-kata yang membawa pendapatMU**, jadi pakai hanya kalau memang itu maksudmu:
- **claims** bisa terdengar seolah kamu meragukan sumbernya.
- **admits** mengesankan sesuatu yang memalukan atau salah (*He admitted taking the money*). Untuk poin wajar yang diakui dalam debat, **concedes** atau **acknowledges** itu netral.
- **shows, proves, demonstrates, points out, refutes** menyatakan bahwa **kamu** menerimanya sebagai kebenaran (*refutes* = membuktikan bahwa itu salah).
- **rightly, wrongly, convincingly, fails to** terang-terangan menilai sumbernya.

Tata bahasa: *reject* dan *dispute* biasanya diikuti kata benda (*rejects the view that …, disputes the figure*); *caution* diikuti *that* atau *against* + -ing; *question* diikuti *whether* atau kata benda.

blocks.text:
Indonesian traps:
- **mengakui** → for a point granted in a debate, *acknowledges / concedes*, not *admits* (which sounds like a confession).
- **membantah** → *denies* for an accusation or a fact (*The company denies leaking the data*); *rejects / disputes* for a view or a figure (*The NGO disputes the figure*).
- **mengatakan** everywhere → *says* everywhere: correct, but flat. Choose the verb that shows the stance.

British vs American spelling: *summarise / summarize*, *programme / program*. Both are fine; be consistent.

id.text:
Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:
- **mengakui** → untuk poin yang diakui dalam debat, pakai *acknowledges / concedes*, bukan *admits* (yang terdengar seperti pengakuan bersalah).
- **membantah** → *denies* untuk tuduhan atau fakta (*The company denies leaking the data*); *rejects / disputes* untuk pandangan atau angka (*The NGO disputes the figure*).
- **mengatakan** di mana-mana → *says* di mana-mana: benar, tapi datar. Pilih kata kerja yang menunjukkan sikapnya.

Ejaan Britania vs Amerika: *summarise / summarize*, *programme / program*. Keduanya benar; pakai secara konsisten.

material.title: Reconstructing an argument without bending it

blocks.text:
To **reconstruct** an argument (menyusun ulang argumen) is to retell it so that its author would say: *Yes, that's what I said.* Five things to keep:
1. **The shape:** claim + reason + condition. *X should happen **because** Y, **unless** Z / **only if** Z / **until** Z.* Drop the condition and you change the claim: *delay the new airport until the environmental study is done* is not *cancel the airport*.
2. **The hedges at the same strength** (a *hedge* is a softening word, from the hedging lesson): *may contribute to* is not *causes*; *appears to* is not *shows*; *tends to* is not *always*; *some* is not *most*. Don't weaken a firm claim either: *will* is not *might*.
3. **The qualifications and scope** (batasan dan cakupan): *for under-25s, in urban areas, in the first year, at the 12 startups in the trial*. A finding about one group is not a finding about everyone.
4. **The counter-arguments the source answers:** if the author writes *Admittedly, the trial was short, but …*, your summary includes it: *The author acknowledges that the trial was short but argues that …*
5. **Only the evidence the source gives:** don't 'improve' an argument with your own reasons or figures.

**Straw man** (orang-orangan sawah): retelling someone's argument as a weaker or more extreme version that is easy to knock down. *He wants to cancel the airport because he's against development* is a straw man of *delay the airport until the environmental study is done*. It's a misrepresentation even when it's accidental, and in a debate it's the first thing the other side will point out.

id.text:
**Merekonstruksi** argumen (menyusun ulang argumen) berarti menceritakannya kembali sehingga penulisnya akan berkata: *Ya, memang itu yang saya katakan.* Lima hal yang harus dipertahankan:
1. **Bentuknya:** klaim + alasan + syarat. *X sebaiknya terjadi **karena** Y, **kecuali jika** Z / **hanya jika** Z / **sampai** Z.* Buang syaratnya, maka klaimnya berubah: *tunda bandara baru sampai kajian lingkungannya selesai* tidak sama dengan *batalkan bandara itu*.
2. **Kata pelunak dengan kekuatan yang sama** (*hedge* = kata yang melunakkan klaim, dari pelajaran hedging): *may contribute to* bukan *causes*; *appears to* bukan *shows*; *tends to* bukan *always*; *some* bukan *most*. Jangan juga melemahkan klaim yang tegas: *will* bukan *might*.
3. **Batasan dan cakupannya**: *for under-25s, in urban areas, in the first year, at the 12 startups in the trial*. Temuan tentang satu kelompok bukan temuan tentang semua orang.
4. **Argumen tandingan yang dijawab sumber itu:** kalau penulis menulis *Admittedly, the trial was short, but …*, ringkasanmu mencantumkannya: *The author acknowledges that the trial was short but argues that …*
5. **Hanya bukti yang diberikan sumbernya:** jangan 'memperbaiki' argumen dengan alasan atau angkamu sendiri.

**Straw man** (orang-orangan sawah): menceritakan ulang argumen seseorang sebagai versi yang lebih lemah atau lebih ekstrem supaya mudah dijatuhkan. *He wants to cancel the airport because he's against development* adalah straw man dari *tunda bandara sampai kajian lingkungannya selesai*. Itu tetap penggambaran yang keliru walaupun tidak disengaja, dan dalam debat, itulah hal pertama yang akan ditunjukkan pihak lain.

blocks.text:
Indonesian traps:
- **bisa** covers *can, may, could* and sometimes *will*. *Bisa menyebabkan* in a source is a hedge (*may / can cause*); don't turn it into *causes*.
- **cenderung** = *tends to*: keep it.
- Watch **semua** and **selalu** creeping in when the source said *banyak* or *sering*.

A quick check: put the original and your sentence side by side and underline every hedge, every number and every *for / in / among / unless / only if* phrase. Each one should still be there.

id.text:
Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:
- **bisa** mencakup *can, may, could* dan kadang *will*. *Bisa menyebabkan* dalam sebuah sumber adalah kata pelunak (*may / can cause*); jangan diubah menjadi *causes*.
- **cenderung** = *tends to*: pertahankan.
- Waspadai **semua** dan **selalu** yang menyusup padahal sumbernya bilang *banyak* atau *sering*.

Cek cepat: taruh kalimat asli dan kalimatmu berdampingan, lalu garis bawahi setiap kata pelunak, setiap angka dan setiap frasa *for / in / among / unless / only if*. Semuanya harus masih ada.

blocks.prompt: A practice study says: 'In Makassar, flexible hours tend to reduce late arrivals among shift workers.' Which summary is accurate?
options: The study shows that flexible hours stop workers arriving late.
The study finds that, in Makassar, flexible hours tend to reduce late arrivals among shift workers.
The study finds that flexible hours tend to reduce late arrivals.
blocks.explain: The middle sentence keeps the **hedge** (*tend to*) and the **scope** (*in Makassar, among shift workers*). The first turns *tend to reduce* into *stop* and *finds* into *shows*: much stronger than the study. The last keeps the hedge but drops the scope, so it seems to be about all workers everywhere.

id.prompt: Sebuah studi latihan menyatakan: 'In Makassar, flexible hours tend to reduce late arrivals among shift workers.' Ringkasan mana yang akurat?
id.explain: Kalimat tengah mempertahankan **kata pelunak** (*tend to*) dan **cakupannya** (*in Makassar, among shift workers*). Kalimat pertama mengubah *tend to reduce* menjadi *stop* dan *finds* menjadi *shows*: jauh lebih kuat daripada studinya. Kalimat terakhir mempertahankan kata pelunaknya tapi membuang cakupannya, sehingga seolah-olah berlaku untuk semua pekerja di mana saja.

material.title: The précis: short, faithful, in your own words

blocks.text:
A **précis** (from French; said **PRAY-see**, plural the same, said **PRAY-seez**; also written *precis*) is a short, accurate summary of **one** text in your own words. A synthesis combines several sources; a précis compresses one. You'll meet it in university assignments, civil-service and diplomatic training, and whenever a manager says *Give me the gist of this report on one page* (*the gist* = intinya).

**The rules:**
- **Length:** often about **a quarter to a third** of the original (a 2,000-word report → roughly 500–650 words). If the task gives a word count, that wins.
- **Same order and proportion:** the main points in the order the author makes them, and a point the author spends half the text on gets about half your précis. (Some university guides let you regroup points if that shows the argument more clearly: follow the task.)
- **Leave out** examples, anecdotes, quotations, repetition and **your own opinions**: no *I think*, no *convincingly*.
- **Third person, present tense** for what the text says: *The author argues …, The report concludes …*. For what a study did, the past is normal: *The researchers surveyed 400 drivers.*
- **Your own words**, but key technical terms and names can stay (*congestion fee, odd-even rule*).

**Method:**
1. **Read** the whole text, then read it again.
2. **Underline** the thesis (the main claim) and the main point of each section.
3. **Outline:** one line per main point, in order.
4. **Draft** from the outline, without looking at the original.
5. **Cut:** examples, repetition, extra detail; join short points with linkers (*because, although, so*).
6. **Check** against the original: the same meaning, hedges, scope and order? The right length?

id.text:
**Précis** (dari bahasa Prancis; dibaca kira-kira **PRÉ-si**, bentuk jamaknya sama, dibaca **PRÉ-siz**; juga ditulis *precis*) adalah ringkasan pendek dan akurat dari **satu** teks dengan kata-katamu sendiri. Sintesis menggabungkan beberapa sumber; précis memadatkan satu sumber. Kamu akan menemuinya di tugas kuliah, pelatihan ASN dan diplomat, dan setiap kali manajer berkata *Give me the gist of this report on one page* (*the gist* = intinya).

**Aturannya:**
- **Panjang:** sering kira-kira **seperempat sampai sepertiga** dari aslinya (laporan 2.000 kata → sekitar 500–650 kata). Kalau tugasnya menyebut jumlah kata, ikuti itu.
- **Urutan dan proporsi yang sama:** poin-poin utama sesuai urutan penulisnya, dan poin yang dibahas penulis di separuh teks mendapat kira-kira separuh précismu. (Sebagian panduan universitas membolehkan poin dikelompokkan ulang kalau itu membuat argumennya lebih jelas: ikuti petunjuk tugasnya.)
- **Buang** contoh, anekdot, kutipan, pengulangan dan **pendapatmu sendiri**: tidak ada *I think*, tidak ada *convincingly*.
- **Orang ketiga, present tense** untuk apa yang dikatakan teks: *The author argues …, The report concludes …*. Untuk apa yang dilakukan sebuah studi, past tense itu wajar: *The researchers surveyed 400 drivers.*
- **Kata-katamu sendiri**, tapi istilah teknis dan nama penting boleh tetap (*congestion fee, odd-even rule*).

**Caranya:**
1. **Baca** seluruh teks, lalu baca sekali lagi.
2. **Garis bawahi** tesisnya (klaim utama) dan poin utama tiap bagian.
3. **Buat kerangka:** satu baris per poin utama, sesuai urutan.
4. **Tulis draf** dari kerangka itu, tanpa melihat teks aslinya.
5. **Pangkas:** contoh, pengulangan, detail tambahan; gabungkan poin-poin pendek dengan kata penghubung (*because, although, so*).
6. **Cek** dengan teks aslinya: makna, kata pelunak, cakupan dan urutannya sama? Panjangnya pas?

blocks.text:
**Précis, abstract or review?** An *abstract* is written by the author to sum up their own paper; a *review* evaluates a text; a *précis* restates someone else's text faithfully, with no evaluation.

Indonesian habit: a school *ringkasan* often copies the key sentence from each paragraph. A précis uses your own sentences, so copy, paste and delete is not enough. And don't start every sentence with *According to the author …*: say it once (*The author argues that …*), then continue (*She adds …, She concludes …*).

id.text:
**Précis, abstrak atau resensi?** *Abstrak* ditulis oleh penulisnya sendiri untuk merangkum papernya; *resensi* (review) menilai sebuah teks; *précis* menyampaikan ulang teks orang lain dengan setia, tanpa penilaian.

Kebiasaan di Indonesia: *ringkasan* di sekolah sering menyalin kalimat utama tiap paragraf. Précis memakai kalimatmu sendiri, jadi salin, tempel lalu hapus tidak cukup. Dan jangan mulai setiap kalimat dengan *According to the author …*: katakan sekali (*The author argues that …*), lalu lanjutkan (*She adds …, She concludes …*).

blocks.prompt: You're writing a précis of a practice report about flood warnings in Semarang. Which sentence belongs in it?

blocks.explain: The middle sentence restates the report's **main claim** in the third person and present tense. The first is a **quotation** and an anecdote, and the last is **your opinion**: a précis leaves out both.

assessment.asum-1: Teks latihan (karangan). Sebuah asosiasi pedagang di Bandung menanggapi rencana larangan kantong plastik sekali pakai di pasar: 'We accept that plastic waste is a serious problem in the city. But paper bags cost three times as much, and our members' margins are already thin.' Pilih kata kerja terbaik dari daftar ini: concedes, rejects, cautions. Ringkasan: 'The traders' association ___ that plastic waste is a serious problem, but argues that paper bags would cost its members three times as much.'
assessment.asum-2: Teks latihan (karangan). Sebuah kelompok lingkungan menulis tentang larangan kantong plastik yang sama: 'Some say the ban will hurt small traders. This is simply not true: the city will give every trader free cloth bags for the first six months.' Pilih kata kerja terbaik dari daftar ini: concedes, rejects, maintains. Ringkasan: 'The environmental group ___ the view that the ban will hurt small traders, pointing to the city's plan to hand out free cloth bags.'
assessment.asum-3: Kamu sedang menulis ringkasan netral dari tiga sumber latihan tentang larangan kantong plastik. Manajermu hanya ingin pandangan sumber-sumbernya, bukan pendapatmu. Ketik SATU kata dalam kalimat ini yang menambahkan pendapatmu sendiri dan harus dibuang: 'The university study rightly cautions that a ban without cheap alternatives could push traders back to plastic within a year.'
assessment.asum-4: Sebuah studi transportasi latihan (karangan) menyatakan: 'In Surabaya, the growth of ride-hailing apps may contribute to falling bus use.' Ringkasan seorang rekan berbunyi: 'The study finds that ride-hailing apps cause falling bus use in Surabaya.' Ketik kata-kata dari teks asli yang seharusnya menggantikan 'cause', supaya ringkasan itu mempertahankan kata pelunak studinya (tiga kata).
assessment.asum-5: Sebuah laporan latihan dari konsultan SDM di Jakarta (karangan) menyatakan: 'Among employees under 30, the four-day week improved staff retention by 12%.' Sebuah ringkasan berbunyi: 'The report finds that the four-day week improved staff retention by 12%.' Ketik batasan yang dihilangkan ringkasan itu (kelompok yang menjadi subjek temuan tersebut), dalam bahasa Inggris.
assessment.asum-6: Dosenmu di Yogyakarta meminta précis dari sebuah artikel latihan tentang kebijakan air sepanjang 1.200 kata, tanpa menyebut jumlah kata. Pilih panjang yang paling cocok dari daftar ini: 100 words, 350 words, 900 words.
assessment.asum-7: Kamu sedang menulis précis dari sebuah artikel opini latihan. Lengkapi dengan bentuk 'argue' yang benar untuk précis: 'The author ___ that Indonesian cities should build fewer flyovers and more bus lanes.'
